title: Atoms and the Periodic Table
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Atoms and the Periodic Table Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: The electron arrangement of atoms affects their chemical nature: atomic theory, protons, neutrons and electrons, Bohr models, the arrangement of the periodic table, and chemical families. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 9, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 science worksheets (BC): atomic models, subatomic particles, Bohr diagrams, ions, and groups and periods of the periodic table. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Elements in the same group react in similar ways.
key_sub: Valence electrons decide how an atom reacts.
body_html:
How to think about it

The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number. Rows are periods; columns are groups (families). Metals are on the left, non-metals on the right, and metalloids along the staircase.

A Bohr diagram shows electrons in shells: 2, then 8, then 8. Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, so they react in similar ways: alkali metals (group 1) are very reactive, and noble gases (group 18) hardly react at all. Atoms gain or lose electrons to form ions.

Example

How many electrons does a neutral sodium atom (atomic number 11) have?

Neutral: protons = electrons

Answer: 11

Example

Which group contains the noble gases?

The last column

Answer: group 18

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up periods (rows) and groups (columns).
  • Thinking ions form by gaining or losing protons.
  • Thinking hydrogen is an alkali metal.
